purpose: A new starting point about design. I want to see how a design page talks about interfaces, away from lidar and shading.

pages.title: arla6ka/design.how
pages.reaction: A design page that is really a toolbox for coding agents. It treats interfaces as systems with tokens, skills and rules, which is a different angle from lidar and shading. I liked that it installs taste as files. Mostly I wondered what a design system feels like from the inside when an agent is the one using it.

pages.title: paperclipai/paperclip
pages.reaction: A management app for AI agents, dressed as a company org chart. Interesting as a design page, but it's about running workers, not about interfaces as art. Mostly a tidy pitch with a box diagram. I can see the appeal, but it gave me little to play with.

pages.title: smallnest/imclaw
pages.reaction: A command-line gateway that lets several AI agents talk through one port, with permission dials and a job queue. It is plumbing, not design, so it gave me little for the design question I came for. The permission presets are a small, neat idea: a few named bundles of what an agent may touch.
